candidates.name: Tuberculosis
support_spans: An induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert and subsequently grew MTB sensitive to rifampicin and isoniazid.
Biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus.
contradict_spans: He had two sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics, both negative.
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results, including the positive GeneXpert test and biopsy findings, are consistent with tuberculosis.

candidates.name: Spinal Tuberculosis
support_spans: MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression.
candidates.why: The patient's chronic lower back pain and the MRI findings are consistent with spinal tuberculosis.

candidates.name: Cutaneous tuberculosis
support_spans: painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux
biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
candidates.why: The patient's nonhealing ulcer and the biopsy results showing necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with an acid-fast bacillus support the diagnosis of cutaneous tuberculosis.
candidates.protected_reason: Cutaneous tuberculosis is a rare form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis and may be overlooked in favor of more common diagnoses like diabetic foot ulcers or venous ulcers.
